How it works

WHAT IS CRITICAL SWIM SPEED?

Critical Swim Speed (CSS) is the fastest pace you can hold for a long swim without tiring quickly: the swimming version of your threshold. It's the most useful number for training in the pool, because it turns every session into a clear target pace per 100 m.

The calculation

CSS = (400 − 200) ÷ (400 m time − 200 m time). Using the difference between two efforts cancels out the push-offs and your sprint speed, so it reflects your real aerobic swimming. We show it as a pace per 100 m.

Using your paces

  • Easy: warm-ups, drills and recovery.
  • Endurance: longer sets that build your aerobic base.
  • Threshold (CSS): sets like 8–10 × 100 m with short rests. The key session for faster triathlon swims.
  • Fast: short, hard repeats with longer rests.

Re-test every 4–6 weeks: as your CSS gets faster, so do all your paces.
